column1: # lexicon.en.tsv - hand-authored evaluative polarity lexicon for folder_valence.py
# WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT
# This is a BOOTSTRAP, not a validated instrument. It exists so folder_valence.py
# can seed a field without vendoring the Warriner norms, which are CC BY-NC-ND 3.0
# and cannot ship under this repository's MIT license (see .gitignore and
# arousal_from_norms.py). Every entry below is a judgement call by the author.
# It is therefore NOT usable as ground truth. Validating the propagation against
# these numbers would be circular: the seeds and the answer would share an origin.
# For a falsifiable run, point --lexicon at a norms-derived table instead and treat
# this file as the fallback it is. TIER1_RESULTS.md §5 is the standard to beat.
# Matching is on lowercased whitespace/punctuation-delimited tokens with a light
# suffix strip (-s, -es, -ed, -ing, -ly). No stemming beyond that: an aggressive
# stemmer collides "abstraction" with "abstract" and the two are not equivalent
# SCOPE NOTE: entries are chosen for evaluative prose about work -- design docs,
# reviews, commit messages, notes. Words that are strongly affective in general
# English but neutral in a software corpus (error, fail, kill, abort, dead, panic,
# critical, blocked) are DELIBERATELY ABSENT here and additionally suppressed by
# TECH_NEUTRAL in folder_valence.py. Including them makes every source tree read
# as miserable; that is the single largest failure mode of lexicon sentiment on
